data.content_ref: inline:The target asserts that the single mechanism best explaining cross-city variation in the nocturnal UHI gap is city size, via aggregation of thermal-mass volume. But the dominant established modulator of nocturnal UHI magnitude across cities is reduced longwave radiative cooling from restricted sky view factor in dense urban geometry, not absolute heat-storage volume. By committing to 'scales directly with city size', the target fails the problem's requirement to identify the mechanism that best explains why the night-time gap is larger in some cities than in others: a compact mid-size city with deep street canyons can exhibit a larger nocturnal UHI than a sprawling, low-density but physically larger city, directly contradicting the proposed direct scaling.
